title: Belarusian — MVD Instruction No. 288 (2008), population register
authority: MVD of Belarus, Resolution No. 288 of 09.10.2008 (reg. 8/19678), Instruction on transliteration of surnames and given names in the population register
description: Instruction of the Belarus MVD (Resolution No. 288 of 09.10.2008) for names in the population register: Г→G, Й→J, Х→KH, Ц→TS, Ў→W; Е Ё Ю Я → JE JO JU JA word-initially, after vowels, Ў, apostrophe or separating Ь/Ъ and IE IO IU IA after consonants; softening Ь shown as an acute (ź ĺ ń ś ć).
notes: Official examples of the table are the samples, except Лябецкая → 'Liabetskaja', which contradicts the table's own rule (Е after a consonant → IE gives Liabietskaja).

The context rules apply to Belarusian spellings. For names transliterated from the Russian form (allowed by p. 2) the table gives Е→E, Ё→E, Ю→IU, Я→IA in all positions and Ъ → J with the following vowel; this scheme always applies the Belarusian rules.

P. 5 prescribes an acute for the softening Ь (дзь dź, зь ź, ль ĺ, нь ń, сь ś, ць ć); the official example Васільева → Vasiljeva shows no acute for a separating Ь, so the acute is only written when Ь is not followed by a vowel. MVD Instruction No. 200 (2010) later banned diacritics in passports, giving e.g. Rudz instead of Rudź.
Status superseded/uncertain: the MFA still publishes this table for passports, but observed passport spellings follow ICAO (be_passport).

rules.note: apostrophe: J with the following vowel
